newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Neighbours back Uighur crackdown-Chinese minister.
newsitem.headline: Neighbours back Uighur crackdown-Chinese minister.

text.p: Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen said the leaders of Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan had promised on Thursday not to give any assistance to Uighur separatists in neighbouring Xinjiang province.
Qian told a news conference that Chinese President Jiang Zemin discussed separatism in Xinjiang with Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev and Kyrgyz President Askar Akayev during talks in Moscow.

"All sides agreed that separatist activities should be stopped by all means in the interests of maintaining peace and stability in the region," Qian said. "This specifically refers to terrorist activities by separatists."
"The presidents of Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan clearly and unequivocally promised that they will not allow (Uighur) separatist activities on their territories," Qian said.
Officials from Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan were not immediately available for comment.
Last year Beijing cracked down on Uighur secessionists after a series of violent clashes, bombings and assassination attempts on officials and Moslem leaders regarded as pro-Beijing.
Uighur exiles in Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan, which share a Turkic language, Islam and a nomadic past, have accused Beijing of wholesale executions of people involved in riots in the province.
Xinjiang officials have dismissed the allegations as "laughable".
China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan earlier on Thursday signed a treaty on troop reductions along the former Soviet-Chinese border.
The treaty aimed at ensuring long-term stability on the 7,500-km-long (4,700-mile) frontier, including limits on troops deployed within the 100-km (63-mile) security zone and a system of inspections.
